OPTION ANCHORS ARE NOT FROM THE DEPOSIT: the xlsx stores bare integers with no value labels, so the two endpoint anchors come from the paper's Methods (JEEHP 2018;15:19, PMC6194478, CC BY 4.0), which reads 'The IRI uses a 5-point scale ranging from 4 (describes me very well) to 0 (does not describe me well)'. They are shipped in the paper's own lower case, verbatim. Note the paper describes a 0-4 coding while the deposit and the IRW table store 1-5; Davis's own IRI guide says 'I use a 0 - 4 item response format ... Other researchers often use a 1-5 format instead', so 1 = does not describe me well and 5 = describes me very well. That is an NC clause with no redistribution bar and no fee, i.e. the same shape as the ECR-R case, so under itemtext_standard.md the open source licence governs and the wording ships -- with wording_rights=NC recorded on every row and a public issues-page entry.
